text:
Asha: Quick heads-up — after today's kernel-selector tweak (auto-fallthrough for tiled->dense) we see a subtle quality regression on llama-13b-v2 evals. Accuracy down ~2.3% on our summarization set.
Tom: Hmm. Latency looks fine in production traces? error rates up or generation drift?
Asha: Latency: p50/p95 unchanged. Token throughput steady. But eval hangs show different attention kernel used after step 0 for long sequences.
Priya: Pastes flame graph snippet:
```
flamegraph: kernel_selector::select -> tiled_attn
  tiled_attn::execute
  tiled_attn::kv_read
  fallback_path: dense_attn (rare)
```
Priya: Also saw KV-cache hit rates drop from 98% -> 71% for warm sessions.
Luca: Do we have a diff for the selector change? commit `c1f9b2a`?
Asha: Yes, selector now prefers tiled when sequence_length % tile_size != 0 to avoid reshuffle. I suspect RoPE window math changed kernel decision and affects position interpolation.
Tom: Could RoPE scaling exponent tweak flip which kernel matches? If tiled uses relative pos assumption vs dense's absolute pos, that might change output.
Priya: Ran a quick local reproduce with our eval harness:
```
# reproduce
python -m eval.runner --model llama-13b-v2 --promptset summarization --seed 42 --profile
```
Priya: Output compares: tiled_attn outputs start diverging at token 12, dense continues baseline. Diff shows shifted pronouns and extra clauses.
Luca: Any quantization toggles in the same rollout? We toggled fast-quant for small-batch path last week.
Asha: No quant changes in this deploy. It's purely selector heuristics + a tiny RoPE scaling fix (multiplier 1.03 -> 0.995) — that combo likely pushed many requests to tiled.
Tom: Ok. Quick mitigation options: 1) Force selector to prefer dense for llama-13b-v2; 2) Revert RoPE multiplier; 3) Canary rollback of selector change.
Priya: I agree. Reproduced locally. I'd favor forcing dense for Llama until we root-cause.
Asha: @Luca can you push a config patch to route llama-13b-v2 -> dense with `models.overrides["llama-13b-v2"].kernel_hint = "dense"` ? We'll do a canary in us-west-2.
Luca: On it. Pushing patch now. Patch: `cfg: 2026-03-17T16:14 c2d9`. Deploy bot will run.
ci-bot: Deploy started: patch c2d9 -> staging -> canary (us-west-2). Rolling out to 10%.
Tom: While canary runs, let's capture KV-cache traces and a a/b of outputs.
Priya: Logged a batch of eval runs against canary endpoint; initial metrics look good — accuracy back within 0.1% of baseline.
Asha: Great. If canary stable for 30m we can promote and then schedule a deep dive on selector heuristics + RoPE math.
Luca: Reverting the underlying selector change in master too? We should land a revert PR and reintroduce after fixes.
Tom: I'll open a revert PR and tag `eng-runtime` for postmortem and test plan.
Asha: Filed the postmortem ticket: INF-4923. We'll include perf profiles, kernel traces, and eval diffs.
ci-bot: Canary promotes to 100% in us-west-2 after checks.
Priya: Thanks everyone — good catch. Next steps: repro matrix across seq lengths [8,16,32,64], tile sizes [32,64], and RoPE multipliers [0.95,1.0,1.05].
Luca: I'll run that matrix overnight and post results in the thread.
Asha: Awesome. Keep updates short here. :thumbsup:
